title: Task Card: Replacement of No. 2 Engine Bleed Air Valve

headings.text: Task Card: Replacement of No. 2 Engine Bleed Air Valve

key_sentences: The crew of flight NW218 reported a BLEED 2 FAULT caution during the climb from Elmsford.
Troubleshooting on arrival confirmed that the valve stayed closed when commanded open.
The valve is to be replaced in accordance with the reference task.
Both duct flanges were found free of cracks and heat damage, with light scoring within the limits of the maintenance manual.
The work recorded on this card has been carried out in accordance with the approved maintenance data, and the aircraft is fit for release in respect of that work.

rows: Open circuit breakers ENG 2 BLEED CTL and ENG 2 BLEED VLV on panel 21VU. Fit safety clips and DO-NOT-CLOSE tags.
Open the right-hand nacelle cowls and install the cowl hold-open rods.
Disconnect the electrical connector from the bleed valve. Cap the connector and the valve receptacle.
Remove the two V-band clamps and the valve. Discard the gaskets.
Inspect the duct flanges for scoring, cracks and heat damage. Record findings in block 6 of this card.
Install the new valve with new gaskets. Position the flow arrow towards the pre-cooler.
Install the V-band clamps and torque to 45–50 lbf·in. Tap around each clamp and re-torque.
Reconnect the electrical connector and lockwire it.
Close the circuit breakers and run the BITE test from the maintenance panel. Test result: PASS, no fault codes stored.
Perform an engine ground run at idle with bleed ON. Check for leaks and that BLEED 2 FAULT does not appear.
Close the cowls and remove all tools, tags and safety clips.

list_items.text: Make sure that engine 2 has been shut down for at least 30 minutes before you open the cowls.
Use heat-resistant gloves when handling bleed ducts and clamps.
Keep the work area clear of loose items while the cowls are open.
